paper.citation: Ye, T., Shao, J., Yi, Y. and Zhao, Q. (2023). Toward better practice of covariate adjustment in analyzing randomized clinical trials. Journal of the American Statistical Association 118(544), 2370-2382. DOI: 10.1080/01621459.2022.2049278.
paper.venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association
paper.source_locator: Section 4.1 'Simulation results', equation (20) on PDF p.23 ('Y (2) = Y (1) + zeta(U - muU), Y (3) = Y (2)'), with the following sentence on the same page defining theta1 = theta2 = theta3 and the allocation proportions. arXiv:2009.11828v2 (13 Jul 2021), 62-page author manuscript.

mechanism.name: Ye-Shao-Yi-Zhao (2023) setting 1: treatment-by-covariate interaction with zero average effect

generation_equations.label: U, W
generation_equations.expression: U, W ~ Normal(0,1) independently (standardised surrogate for the trial's empirical distribution)

generation_equations.label: Potential responses
generation_equations.expression: Y(1) = eps, Y(2) = Y(1) + zeta (U - muU), zeta = 1, muU = 0

generation_equations.label: Heterogeneity
generation_equations.expression: tau(U) = zeta (U - muU) = U, with E[tau(U)] = 0

generation_equations.label: Observed
generation_equations.expression: Y = A Y(2) + (1-A) Y(1) = eps + A tau(U)

assumptions: SUTVA: one version of treatment, no interference between patients
Randomised assignment: e = 0.5, so the treatment is independent of the potential responses by design
The baseline response Y(1) is independent of (U,W) in this package, which is the declared surrogate for the source's near-zero R-squared

properties.notes: Two baseline covariates but only U enters the effect, so effective dimension is 1. The interaction is treatment-by-covariate (A x U), which is the object the source studies through the coefficient zeta. The surface is affine, with zero mean over the covariate law: heterogeneity without an average effect.

estimand.name: tau(u0) = E[Y(1) - Y(0) | U = u0]
estimand.definition: Conditional average treatment effect at the declared query points for the arm-2 versus arm-1 contrast; the surface is linear in U with slope zeta = 1 and has exactly zero mean over the covariate distribution, so there is heterogeneity but no average effect.

truth.expression: Conditional average treatment effect at the declared query points for the arm-2 versus arm-1 contrast; the surface is linear in U with slope zeta = 1 and has exactly zero mean over the covariate distribution, so there is heterogeneity but no average effect.
truth.derivation: Closed form: the contrast in equation (20) is zeta (U - muU), so with muU = 0 and zeta = 1 the surface is tau(u) = u exactly; cross-checked by a second typing and by the realised outcome column.

adaptations: Three arms reduced to two: only the arm-2 versus arm-1 contrast is kept, because the registered target family is the binary-treatment CATE. The contrast surface is exactly the increment in equation (20).

Y(1) in the source is the observed placebo-arm response of 481 real patients and is not distributed with the paper; this package replaces it with independent N(0,1) noise. The source reports R-squared <= 0.05 for a linear fit of Y(1) on (U,W), so the replacement preserves the near-independence of the baseline response from the covariates; it does change the paper's beta1 = -0.255 to 0 and this is a declared deviation.

(U,W) in the source follow the empirical distribution of the same 481 patients; this package uses U, W ~ N(0,1) with muU = muW = 0 and E[U^2] = 1, i.e. the paper's centring constants are set to their standardised values.
The source uses allocation 1:2:2 or 1:1:1 over three arms; this package uses simple randomisation with two arms at 1:1, so e = 0.5.
The source varies zeta over [-1, 1]; this package fixes zeta = 1 as the single declared scenario.
